pluss::note::empty_bytes_like¶

Back to Note Factory API Reference

Signatures¶

Note pluss::note::empty_bytes_like(const Note& like)

Another Note’s Shape, Empty, In Bytes Mode¶

empty_bytes_like() returns a fresh bytes-mode Note (encoding=bytes) shaped exactly like like, with every cell holding the empty byte string. It is full_bytes_like(like, "").

Use it to stage a same-shaped bytes buffer beside a Note you already have — somewhere to assemble binary output row by row, a bytes-mode reset copy, an accumulator congruent with a text input. Every cell is a valid zero-length byte string, so the result is immediately usable; unwritten cells read as empty.

Only the shape of like is read; its contents and its own encoding do not matter. The result is always bytes mode. For a UTF-8-mode blank buffer, use empty_like.

like must be a defined Note. The result is independent of like.

Example 1: A Same-Shaped Empty Bytes Buffer¶

const auto grid = pluss::note::make({{"a", "b", "c"}, {"d", "e", "f"}});
const pluss::Note buf = pluss::note::empty_bytes_like(grid);
pluss::note::print(std::cout, buf) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 3], dim=2, numel=6, encoding=bytes)
[
  [b"", b"", b""], 
  [b"", b"", b""]
]

Shape [2, 3] borrowed from grid; every cell an empty byte string, and the Note is in bytes mode (b"", not "").
